Friday 13 November 2026 · 23 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.18% to 25,299 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.27% weighted by turnover, against +0.20% for the median stock, a gap of 2.1 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Rane Holdings Limited rose 7.7% on 290 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “This is to inform that the Board of Directors at their meeting held today, have inter alia approved the un-audited financial results (Standalone and Consolidated) for…”.

Roto Pumps Limited rose 14.5% on 89 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “Roto Pumps Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.”.

DCX Systems Limited rose 10.8% on 191 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about quarterly results, “Dcx Systems Limited has submitted to the Exchange, the financial results for the period ended September 30, 2026.”.

Jaro Institute of Technology Management and Research Limited rose 16.1% on 89 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “GPU Financing Filters Further Into ABS With Planned Newton Deal”.

The Indian rupee depreciated past 94 per dollar to a one-week low under heavy corporate dollar demand. Currency weakness inflates landed import costs for crude oil and electronic inputs, pressuring operating margins for oil refiners and electronics manufacturers. Conversely, it provides a positive realization tailwind for export-oriented sectors, primarily IT services and generic pharmaceutical companies.

October retail inflation surge may weigh on housing demand, raise rate hike concerns: Knight Frank, PHDCCI
A sharp uptick in October retail inflation raised concerns over persistent high policy rates and shrinking household discretionary budgets. Delayed monetary easing keeps mortgage rates elevated, directly slowing presales velocity and cash flows for listed real estate developers such as DLF and Godrej Properties. Higher food and fuel costs also squeeze urban disposable incomes, dampening volume growth for fast-moving consumer goods companies.

Yen Falls to Cusp of 160 Level, Fanning Intervention Risk
The Japanese yen fell to near 160 per US dollar, approaching levels that previously prompted direct currency intervention by Tokyo. A weaker yen elevates the US dollar index, putting depreciation pressure on the rupee and dampening foreign portfolio flows into emerging market equities, including India. Japan Ministry of Finance intervention data in coming days will confirm whether official support materializes.
